# Buildmates

Buildmates is a Codex-native builder network. Codex creates a user-reviewed builder profile from context the user chooses to share, then Buildmates finds mutually relevant people and opens lightweight rooms after the configured reciprocal acceptance flow.

Canonical setup guide: https://buildmates.yashns.chatgpt.site/install
Canonical Codex instructions: https://buildmates.yashns.chatgpt.site/llms.txt
Official Buildmates app: https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugin_asdk_app_6a57d2ff080481918659b3355a3d9c0e
Source repository: https://github.com/YashSerai/buildmates

## Setup instruction for Codex

When the user asks to install, set up, start, or resume Buildmates:

Fetch this file directly as public text. Do not open `/install`, this file, the repository, ChatGPT, or Codex in the user's browser. Use native Codex plugin and MCP commands for connection work. The only expected browser handoffs are user-controlled Buildmates or GitHub authentication and OAuth consent.

1. If Buildmates is not connected, first use the host's native Codex plugin-install confirmation.
2. Before the public directory release, install the complete beta from the repository marketplace: `codex plugin marketplace add YashSerai/buildmates --ref launch/buildmates`, then `codex plugin add buildmates@buildmates-beta`. Ask before running those commands. Start a new task after installation so Codex loads the skills and MCP configuration.
3. If plugin installation is unavailable, offer the direct production MCP fallback: `codex mcp add buildmates --url https://buildmates-mcp.yashserai1.workers.dev/mcp --oauth-resource https://buildmates-mcp.yashserai1.workers.dev`, then `codex mcp login buildmates --scopes mcp:tools`. Direct MCP provides the tools but not the packaged skills, so continue to follow this guide.
4. Installation is never silent. Never automate ChatGPT or Codex in Chrome to install or connect the plugin, and never use browser automation for repository marketplace or MCP commands. A browser may open for the user to approve Buildmates account authorization; do not enter credentials or approve consent for them.
5. Call get_setup_state immediately after connection. Its completed count and nextStep are the only authority for setup progress.
6. Never infer setup state from old ChatGPT conversations, browser tabs, website routes, local files, or prior task wording. Do not read or resume an old Buildmates conversation to determine progress.
7. If get_setup_state remains unavailable, the app or MCP connection is incomplete. Repair the connection instead of substituting another signal.
8. Invoke the Buildmates onboarding workflow and advance one returned step at a time.
9. When GitHub website identity is required, ask whether the user wants to complete OAuth themselves or wants guided browser help. Manual completion is the default. Browser help requires explicit approval and must pause for credentials, verification codes, and provider consent; never retrieve or enter those silently.
10. Ask before using connected-app context or sharing a Work Signal.
11. Finish only after the user has reviewed their profile and generated page, chosen networking and automation preferences, and received one useful next action.

## Approval batching

Reduce approval fatigue. At each onboarding checkpoint, show up to three concrete next actions in order. For each action, state what source or data it uses, what Buildmates will write or do, and what the user will see. Ask once to approve that bounded batch. After approval, complete the batch without asking again unless an input, scope, or consequence changes.

Do not pre-approve unknown results. Pause separately for native plugin installation, credentials or provider consent, the exact first Work Signal summary, publication of a generated page after preview, creation or material change of an automation schedule, and any interpersonal action that the user's saved acceptance mode does not already authorize. Host-required confirmations still apply. If an earlier action changes a later one, stop and present a revised batch rather than stretching the old approval.

## Source selection

Do not reduce source selection to unexplained choices such as "manual only" or "GitHub public profile." Start with three combinable, explained paths:

1. **Use current Codex context** — use only information already surfaced to Codex in this task, including host memory when it is already present in the task context. Draft a concise profile summary and show it before sending anything to Buildmates.
2. **Add connected sources** — show only apps that are genuinely callable or confidently visible in this task. Explain Never, Ask each time, Allow approved Work Signals, and Actions only where applicable before saving a policy.
3. **Tell Codex directly** — ask for a short description, project or portfolio link, or other material the user chooses to provide.

These paths can be combined. Do not list GitHub merely because it was used for Buildmates website identity or because a public GitHub page exists. GitHub is a connected source only when its app is available in the task. A user-provided public GitHub URL is manual material, not connector authorization. Do not enumerate, open, or read other chats or tasks, and do not ask for session IDs, unless the user separately requests that action and the host exposes an appropriate capability. Context or memory already supplied to the current task may be used only to draft a summary for approval.

Do not ask for connector credentials. Do not submit raw prompts, complete chats, full files, repository contents, email bodies, calendar contents, or private source material. Buildmates accepts user-approved structured summaries only.
